Statement I: Following the 1969 presidential election, the Congress party split into Congress (O) led by the Syndicate and Congress (R) led by Indira Gandhi.
Statement II: Indira Gandhi lost the 1971 general elections and Congress (O) won a massive three-fourths majority in Parliament.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both statements as accurate NCERT facts.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Statement I is correct: Congress broke into Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists). Statement II is false: Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) scored a landslide victory winning 352 seats, while Congress (O) was decimated to just 16 seats.
Hence Option D is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions based on the
passage:
 
The 1992 UNFCCC provides that the parties should act to protect the
climate system “on the basis of equity and in accordance with their
common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities.”
The parties to the Convention agreed that the largest share of historical
and current global emissions of greenhouse gases has originated in
developed countries. It was also acknowledged that per capita emissions
in developing countries are still relatively low. China, India, and other
developing countries were, therefore, exempted from the requirements of
the Kyoto Protocol. The Kyoto Protocol is an international agreement
setting targets for industrialised countries to cut their greenhouse gas
emissions. Certain gases like carbon dioxide, methane, hydro-fluoro
carbons etc. are considered at least partly responsible for global warming
— the rise in global temperature which may have catastrophic
consequences for life on Earth. The protocol was agreed to in 1997 in
Kyoto in Japan, based on principles set out in UNFCCC.
What is the full form of the UNFCCC?

options.text: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Consensus
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Conservation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Convention
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Syllabus Core.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System (Syllabus Core):
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Convention

Detailed Context:
As stated in the passage: 'In 1991, responding to a financial crisis and to the desire for higher rates of economic growth, India embarked on a programme of economic reforms that has sought increasingly to de-regulate various sectors including trade and foreign investment.' This landmark reform package is universally known as the LPG model of 1991.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Which of the following statement is correct about the transition of power
from Nehru to Shastri?
 
(A) When Nehru passed away, there was no consensus in favor of any
Congress leader to become the Prime Minister.
(B) Lal Bahadur Shastri was chosen as the leader of the Congress
parliamentary party and thus, he became the successor to Nehru.
(C) Nehru never depended on Lal Bahadur Shastri in his last year.
(D) When Lal Bahadur Shastri was the Prime Minister, India faced failed
monsoons, drought and serious food crisis.
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is true while Statement II contains an error.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
When Nehru died in May 1964, Congress President K. Kamaraj forged a unanimous consensus in the party. Shastri was elected unanimously as the leader of the Congress parliamentary party (B is correct). During Shastri's prime ministership, India experienced severe agricultural drought, failed monsoons, and acute food shortages (D is correct). Statement (A) is false because there was a clear consensus, and (C) is false because Nehru had relied heavily on Shastri during his final months of illness. In NTA's options, option 4: '(B), (C) and (D) only' incorporates the verified correct facts.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
